incidents.cause: The loss of engine power during an agricultural application flight due to a cylinder failure.
Total loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
The pilot’s improper decision to continue the takeoff with a tailwind after he recognized a performance problem with the airplane and his delayed action to dump the chemical load.
Failure of the pilot to maintain an adequate airspeed resulting in an aerodynamic stall/spin while maneuvering.
The pilot’s failure to obtain a proper touch down location on a wet grass runway, resulting in a runway overrun and impact with terrain.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper application of brakes.

The flight instructor’s delayed remedial action and inadequate supervision during a practice autorotation, which resulted in a failure to maintain adequate main rotor rpm. Contributing to the accident was the wet landing surface.
A loss of engine power due to a failure of the magnetos as a result of inadequate maintenance.
A higher than expected and accounted for crosswind which initiated a lateral deviation, and resulted in the aircraft reaching the limits of the geo-fence area triggering a contingency forced landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain helicopter control while in a low hover.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane during the landing roll. Contributing to the accident was the fatigue of the left main landing gear assembly.

The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control and adequate airspeed during takeoff which resulted in a collision with a river. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s improper decision to load the airplane above its maximum allowable gross weight.

An inflight collision with terrain under unknown circumstances.
